comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions across two reportable segments: semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software, serving markets including AI networking, data centers, and enterprise IT.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom explicitly define their reportable segments in Item 8. AMD discloses four reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded) in NOTE 4, whereas Broadcom reports two reportable segments (semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software). Both disclosures serve to define the organizational structure for financial reporting purposes, though the granularity and market focus differ significantly.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose the designation of their reportable operating segments in Item 8. AMD identifies four segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded), while Intel identifies three reportable operating segments (CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry) and notes that other units (NEX, Altera, Mobileye) are non-reportable. Both companies use these definitions to structure their segment reporting under ASC 280.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute & Networking segment includes the Data Center accelerated computing platform, networking, automotive AI cockpit and autonomous driving solutions, electric vehicle computing platforms, Jetson for robotics, NVIDIA AI Enterprise software, and DGX Cloud.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA disclose the composition of their reportable segments in Item 8. AMD's Data Center segment includes AI accelerators, CPUs, and GPUs for data centers. NVIDIA’s Compute & Networking segment includes Data Center accelerated computing platforms and networking. Both companies include AI-related products and data center infrastructure as a core part of their primary segment definitions, reflecting the shared industry focus on AI hardware.
